TYPE 1 ZONING MAP AMENDMENT
Substitute Narrative, Analysis, and Plans
1447-1457 West Fillmore Street
B3-2 District to B2-3 District (Type 1)

ACorners, LLC is the “Applicant” for a Type 1 Zoning Map Amendment for the subject property located at
1447-1457 West Fillmore Street from the B3-2 Community Shopping District to the B2-3 Neighborhood
Mixed-Use District in order to construct a new residential development.

The subject property is bounded by West Fillmore Street on the north, residential property on the east, a
12-foot public alley on the south, and South Laflin Street on the west. The subject property contains
approximately 15,975 square feet of site area and is improved with a surface parking lot with two existing
curb cuts onto South Laflin Street.** The subject property is a transit-served location based on its proximity
to the CTA Pink Line station entrance at Polk Street and the Roosevelt Road bus corridor.

The Applicant proposes to develop the site with a 5-story residential building containing 50 dwelling units,
50 bicycle parking spaces, and no commercial space. The proposed development will include 25 vehicular
parking spaces. The overall FAR will be 4. The Applicant seeks all relief necessary, as allowed by the
Chicago Zoning Ordinance, for the attached plans.

* The property is a transit-served location due to its proximity within 2,640 feet from the CTA Pink Line
station entrance at Polk Street and within 1,320 feet from the Roosevelt Road CTA bus line corridor roadway
segment. The Applicant seeks an FAR increase to 4 and a building height increase for a transit-served
location. The project will provide 100% of the required ARO units on site.

* Pursuant to Section 17-13-0303-D of the Chicago Zoning Ordinance, as part of this Type 1 Zoning Map
Amendment, the Applicant seeks (1) an administrative adjustment to permit the building fagade to be
located more than 5 feet from the sidewalk on West Fillmore Street; (2) an administrative adjustment to
allow a building without a primary entrance door facing the pedestrian street; (3) an administrative
adjustment to allow vehicle access to the lot from the pedestrian street; (4) a variation to reduce the required
off-street loading from one space to zero spaces; (5) a variation to reduce the minimum required rear
setback for floors containing dwelling units from 30 feet to 0 feet; and (6) a variation to reduce the required
front yard setback for lots abutting R-zoned lots that have frontage on the same street from 3.55 feet to 0
feet.
